title: As you made it
did: Nothing: the song as it is, at the same loudness as the others.

title: Slower
did: Played 20% slower; the pitch stays the same.
feel: Heavier and dragging, like the carnival is winding down.
use: Every fight, if the original feels too quick for turn-based battles.

title: Lower
did: Moved down three half-steps; the speed stays the same.
feel: Darker and deeper; the music box sounds older and heavier.
use: Boss fights, so they sound darker than ordinary ones.

title: Slowed and in a big room
did: Played slower like a record turned down (15%, so it is also lower), in a big echoing room.
feel: Dreamy, ghostly and far off: the "slowed and reverb" sound.
use: A witch’s trance, Curtain Call, or the quiet after a fight is won.

title: From far away
did: The highs cut away and a lot of echo, as if heard through fog or a wall.
feel: Soft, muffled, in the background; tense rather than loud.
use: While you choose a move, then back to full when a blow lands; or when a witch is nearly beaten.

title: Warped tape
did: Two half-steps lower with a slow, wavering wobble, like an old tape or a music box running down.
feel: Unsettling and haunted: the carnival is wrong somehow.
use: Shadow wraiths and the final boss.

title: Dark mix (my pick for battles)
did: A little of each: 12% slower, two half-steps lower, the harshest highs softened, a faint wobble and a medium room.
feel: Still Carnival of Ashes, still has a beat, but darker, heavier and more ethereal.
use: Every fight, quietly in the background.
